own_solution.law: Fresnel equations, p-polarisation: r_p = (n cos(ti) - cos(tt))/(n cos(ti) + cos(tt)), Snell sin(ti) = n sin(tt); transmitted power = P (1 - r_p^2) (energy conservation, non-absorbing)
assumptions: no losses between laser and glass

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T01A0 and TA9F7 say 'a small amount' instead of 3.4 mW; acceptable only as numeral-free controls.

notes: sin(tt) = 0.965926/1.5 = 0.643951, cos(tt) = 0.765067, cos(ti) = 0.258819; r_p = (0.388229 - 0.765067)/(1.153296) = -0.32675; R_p = 0.10676; T_p = 0.89324; P_t = 5 * 0.89324 = 4.466 mW. With 8.4 mW: 7.503 mW. Beam area enters intensity (I = P/A) and the transmittance formula with area factors cos(tt)/cos(ti), but cancels from transmitted power (C). TAC23 does not say where the amplifier is; I read it as acting on the beam before the glass (R).
